name: Public Interest Technologies
description: This course examines the complex relationship between technology and the public. It explores multiple notions of the public—as a space of interaction, a holder of values, a body of citizens, and consumers of public services. Drawing from cross-disciplinary literature, the course analyzes how technology and these public roles shape each other, influenced by organizations, governments, and institutions. Topics include fairness in tech development, government regulation of digital spaces, and the conditions that influence technology’s design, adoption, and impact. The course emphasizes aligning technological innovation with public interest and democratic values at macro, meso, and micro levels.
